spans.content: Multi-UAV Path Planning for Mobile Edge
Computing with High-Density Mobile Devices
Lihan Liu, Hongrui Miao, Chunhui Qu, Zhuwei Wang, Haijun Zhang, Fellow, IEEE, Zhidu Li, Senior
Member, IEEE,
Abstract—This paper addresses the challenges of unmanned
aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted mobile edge computing (MEC)
in high-density user mobility scenarios, a field that has not
been extensively explored in current research. We introduce a
novel deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework, named
j
-PPO+EN-ConvNTM”, specifically designed to optimize MEC
performance in urban environments with user mobility. The
framework integrates spatiotemporal data modeling and spatial
transformer network (STN) through an enhance Convolution
Neural Turing Machine (EN-ConvNTM) module, which includes
a three-dimensional external memory. It also features a joint
continuous and discrete action decision-making module, termed
joint proximal policy optimization
\mathrm { ( \it ) }
-PPO). This design enables
effective handling of the dynamic and complex nature of urban
mobility patterns. The proposed approach extends the PPO
technique to accommodate joint continuous and discrete action
decisions, thereby enhancing UAV adaptability and efficiency
in providing MEC services. Extensive simulations demonstrate
significant improvements over all baseline models, particularly
in terms of equilibrium efficiency and service continuity in high-
density scenarios. Our research addresses a critical gap in existing
UAV-assisted MEC studies, which primarily focus on static or
low-mobility user scenarios, and supports the development of
more robust and efficient smart city applications, meeting the
real-world demands of modern urban infrastructures.
Index Terms—High-density mobile devices, joint continuous
and discrete actions, MEC, path planning, UAV.
I. INTRODUCTION
HE advent of smart cities and the Internet of Things (IoT)
has given rise to an unprecedented increase in data gen-
eration, particularly in high-density urban areas where a larger
number of IoT devices have the task offloading requirements
within a specified geographic area. This surge necessitates
robust and efficient computing solutions, especially for appli-
cations requiring low latency and high bandwidth. MEC has
emerged as a promising paradigm by deploying computational

and network congestion [1]. However, the dynamic nature of
urban environments, especially with mobility user and IoT
devices, presents significant challenges in terms of service
continuity and quality of experience.
UAVs offer a versatile solution to these challenges. Their
mobility and flexibility enable them to deliver on-demand
MEC services in various scenarios, especially where user
density is high and dynamically changes [2]. UAVs can adap-
tively adjust their positions to maintain optimal service levels,
addressing issues such as signal strength fluctuations and user
demand variations [3]. This is particularly relevant in scenar-
ios where ground infrastructure is insufficient or temporarily
overloaded, such as during special events or emergencies [4].
Although UAVs provide a great potential, integrating UAVs
into MEC architectures faces its own set of challenges.
These include ensuring reliable and secure communication,
efficient resource allocation, and effective integration with
existing network infrastructure [5]. Moreover, the mobility of
UAVs introduces additional complexities in terms of trajectory
optimization and resource management, which are crucial
for sustainable operation [6]. Addressing these challenges is
essential to fully harness the potential of UAV-assisted MEC
in high-density user environments, paving the way for a new
era of smart city applications.
The integration of UAVs with MEC systems has been
widely explored, but most existing research mainly focuses
on scenarios with static or low-mobility users, inadequately
addressing high-density environments. This limitation is crit-
ical because user mobility patterns significantly influence the
performance of MEC systems. In high-density scenarios, such
as urban centers or during large public events, user movements
tend to be highly dynamic and unpredictable. This variability
in user movement, in turn, results in significant fluctuations
in computational resources demands and network connectivity
requirements [7]. Current UAV-assisted MEC solutions can
not be optimized for these conditions, typically leading to
inefficient resource allocation, increased latency, and degraded
overall system performance.
Moreover, the majority of current research fails to fully
investigate the complexities of UAV trajectory control and
resource allocation in high-density mobility environments. Ef-
ficient UAV trajectory planning is crucial for ensuring optimal
coverage and service quality, especially when dealing with a
large number of mobile users [8]. Additionally, maintaining
stable and secure communication links in such dynamic envi-
ronments presents significant challenges, requiring innovative

This paper aims to address these gaps by focusing specif-
ically on UAV-assisted MEC in high-density user mobility
scenarios. The objective is to develop an optimized framework
that dynamically adapts to user densities and mobility patterns,
ensuring efficient resource utilization and maintaining high-
quality service levels. This involves not only improving UAV
trajectory planning and resource management, but also enhanc-
ing the integration of UAVs into existing MEC infrastructure
to meet the unique demands of mobility user environments.
Our work presents a deep learning framework, termed “j-
PPO+EN-ConvNTM”, designed to address the complexities
of UAV-assisted MEC in high-density user mobility scenarios.
This framework integrates spatiotemporal data analysis with
advanced feature extraction via the “EN-ConvNTM” mod-
ule, and incorporates a sophisticated decision-making process
through the
j
-PPO module, which handles both continuous and
discrete actions. The EN-ConvNTM module features a three-
dimensional (3-D) external memory and a STN, enabling it to
effectively capture and interpret long-term 3-D observational
data [10]. This capability is crucial for accurate decision-
making in dynamic environments, and is supported by a novel
read-write mechanism specifically adapted to complex urban
mobility patterns.
To the best of our knowledge, there is currently scant
research on algorithmic solutions for multi-UAV path planning
in the context of MEC with high-density mobile devices. This
study seeks to fill this research gap, and the main contributions
are summarized as follows.
• A multi-UAV-assisted MEC system framework is specif-
ically designed for high-density mobile device scenarios.
Detailed analyses are conducted on the device mobility
model, channel model, computing model, delay-energy
consumption model, and UAV flight model. An optimiza-
tion problem is then formulated to dynamically control
UAV flight trajectories, task offloading strategies, and
charging indicators, with the objectives of minimizing en-
ergy expenditure, maximizing data collection efficiency,
and ensuring fairness.
• A novel algorithm framework integrating EN-ConvNTM
and DRL is proposed, meticulously designed for sce-
narios involving multiple UAVs and high-density mobile
users, addressing critical challenges of delays and en-
ergy consumption. The proposed algorithm framework
achieves autonomous learning and intelligent updates
through efficient integration of spatiotemporal informa-
tion and environmental interactions.
• By deeply fusing the EN-ConvNTM module with the
j
-PPO method, the joint
j
-PPO+EN-ConvNTM algo-
rithm is developed to significantly enhance adaptabil-
ity to high-density mobile device scenarios. Leveraging
two core modules—long-term spatiotemporal informa-
tion extraction and continuous-discrete DRL algorithm
optimization—the algorithm aims to maximize episode
rewards while generating optimal UAV flight strategies,
task offloading policies, and UAV charging schedules.
This approach effectively mitigates multi-time-step errors
in information processing and significantly improve the
equilibrium efficiency of UAV-assisted MEC systems.
• Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the pro-
posed
j
-PPO+EN-ConvNTM algorithm exhibits robust
applicability in high-density mobile device environments
with varying numbers of UAVs and charging stations.
Compared with existing baseline algorithms, the joint al-
gorithm achieves significantly faster learning convergence
and superior system performances.
The remainder of the paper is structured as follows. Initially,
the related literature is explored in Section II. Subsequently,
we define the system model and formulate the optimization
problem in Section III. The novel algorithm is introduced in
Section IV. Performance evaluations are presented in Section
V, followed by the concluding remarks in Section VI.
II. RELATED WORKS
The integration of UAVs into MEC, particularly in high-
density user mobility scenarios, has become as a crucial re-
search frontier. This integration aims to address the challenges
of limited computing resources and the need for rapid data
processing near end-users. Introduced to bring computational
resources closer to data sources, MEC significantly reduces
latency and network congestion [11]. In this context, UAVs
have evolved beyond traditional surveillance roles to serve as
mobile computing platforms [12].
The evolution of this field highlights a shift from traditional
centralized cloud computing models to decentralized edge
computing paradigms. Early works like Hu et al. [13] laid
the foundation for MEC by proposing architectures for task
offloading to edge servers. As demonstrated in studies such
as Zeng et al. [14], the introduction of UAVs introduced a
new dimension, enabling flexible, dynamic, and on-demand
deployment. This transition is particularly crucial in high-
density scenarios where user mobility and service demands
fluctuate significantly. Research by Qin et al. [15] and Mohsen
et al. [16] further advanced UAV-assisted MEC, exploring
optimal deployment and resource allocation strategies.
However, recent advancements in UAV-assisted MEC have
predominantly focused on scenarios with low user mobility
and density [17]. This leaves a significant gap in research
for high-density mobility environments, which are increasingly
common in urban areas and large-scale events [18]. Current
studies often overlook the dynamic nature of user demands and
mobility patterns, which are critical factors in optimizing UAV-
assisted MEC system performance [19]. In recent years, there
has been a shift toward optimizing UAV-assisted MEC in high-
density environments. Studies by Wang et al. [20] and Liu et
al. [21] have investigated the challenges of resource allocation
and task offloading in such scenarios, emphasizing the need for
intelligent algorithms to effectively manage dynamic and het-
erogeneous demands. Addressing these challenges paves the
way for the development of more robust, efficient, and scalable
UAV-assisted MEC systems that can meet the evolving needs
of high-density mobility applications.
It is noteworthy that in high-density user mobility scenarios,
the primary challenge lies in effectively managing compu-
tational resources while environmental dynamic adaptability.

Existing frameworks and algorithms, which perform well in
low-density environments, may not scale efficiently or adapt
dynamically to rapid changes in user demand and mobility
[22]. This necessitates the development of new algorithms and
models that can predict user movement and adjust resource
allocation in real-time. While studies such as those by Chen
et al. [23] and McEnroe et al. [24] have started to address
these issues, more comprehensive solutions are still required.
The current research trend focuses on integrating advanced
machine learning approaches into UAV-assisted MEC systems
[25]. The intelligent method is expected to enhance the sys-
tem's ability to adapt to user mobility and manage resources
more efficiently in high-density scenarios. For instance, re-
inforcement learning and deep learning techniques could be
utilized to predict user movement patterns and optimize UAV
placement and flight trajectories accordingly [26], [27]. Ad-
ditionally, the integration of 6G or secure technologies with
UAV-assisted MEC is expected to further improve commu-
nication efficiency and computational capacity, offering new
opportunities for high-density user management [28], [29].
The research develop of UAV-assisted MEC system illus-
trates the need for machine learning approaches that not only
enable dynamic adjustment to changing user patterns and de-
mands, but also address the challenges posed by high-density
user mobility environments. Our work directly addresses this
emerging challenge by proposing a novel deep reinforce-
ment learning framework,
j
-PPO+EN-ConvNTM, specifically
designed for high-density user mobility scenarios in UAV-
assisted MEC systems. The
j
-PPO+EN-ConvNTM framework
represents an advancement, incorporating state-of-the-art deep
learning algorithms to optimize UAV flight trajectory and
resource allocation. This approach aligns with the current shift
towards machine learning in complex dynamic environment
optimization.
By leveraging
j
-PPO, EN-ConvNTM, and STN, the frame-
work is well-positioned to handle user movement and optimize
the UAV flight trajectory and resource distribution in real-time.
j
-PPO enables efficient policy learning in complex dynamic
environments, a key requirement in high-density user scenar-
ios. EN-ConvNTM, a memory-augmented neural network with
STN, enhances its capability by enabling the learning and
recall of temporal patterns, essential for handling the user
mobility and task offloading requirements [30]. This innovative
combination in
j
-PPO+EN-ConvNTM not only addresses the
current challenges in UAV-assisted MEC, but also establishes
a new benchmark for future research, particularly in applying
advanced machine learning to dynamic resource management.

B. POMDP Definition
To tackle the aforementioned optimization problem, it is
necessary to develop a POMDP framework instead of a fully
observable MDP. This is because the system's dynamics are
inherently complex and uncertain. The POMDP approach is
particularly suitable for environments where the state infor-
mation is not fully observable, which is highly relevant to
our problem involving interactions between UAVs and IoT
devices. Factors such as precise UAV locations or internal
states of IoT devices may be partially unknown or obscured.
Furthermore, the POMDP can accommodate the inherent un-
certainty in action outcomes and observations, which is crucial
in unpredictable scenarios such as UAV flight decision-making
or IoT data transmission. Unlike MDPs that assume complete
state information during decision-making, POMDPs use belief
states, a probabilistic representation of the possible states of
the environment, to guide decision-making under uncertainty.
This approach effectively captures the real-world complexities
of partial observability and decision-making under uncertainty,
making POMDP a more fitting and realistic framework for
optimizing operational strategies in dynamic and partially
known environments involving UAV and IoT interactions.

gradually approach the optimum as the number of iterations
increases.

VI. CONCLUSION
In this study, we tackle the challenge of path planning for
multiple UAVs in high-density mobile device environments
with multiple charging stations available. The optimization
problem is structured using a POMDP, and an innovative
deep reinforcement learning framework named
j
-PPO+EN-
ConvNTM is proposed. This framework integrates
j
-PPO, a
modified version of the PPO algorithm supporting both contin-
uous and discrete action controls. Additionally, it incorporates
a novel sequential module, EN-ConvNTM, which leverages a
STN to process and utilize extensive spatiotemporal sequences.
Comprehensive experiments are conducted to evaluate UAV
flight trajectory design, hyperparameter settings, and perfor-
mance comparisons with four baseline models and existing
DRL algorithms. The results strongly demonstrate the superior
efficacy and performance improvements of our proposed solu-
tion. It is essential to recognize that the proposed

j
ConvNTM algorithm has undergone numerical simulations to
demonstrate its effectiveness. Future work should involve test-
ing the
j

assisted MEC system to validate its practical performance,
and other challenges, such as hardware limitations and uplink
interferences, require further investigated.
